newsitem.title: UK: ISO sees 1996/97 world sugar output at 123.8 mln T.
newsitem.headline: ISO sees 1996/97 world sugar output at 123.8 mln T.

text.p: World sugar production should reach 123.8 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97, up 200,000 tonnes on 1995/96, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said in its September market report. "Our first estimates for 1996/97 show world production consolidating at the level achieved in the previous cycle of around 124 million tonnes," the ISO said. Export availabilities were expected to be broadly unchanged at 34.2 million tonnes after 34.1 million in 1995/96 but global consumption would rise by 2.7 million tonnes to 121.3 million, leaving a statistical surplus of 2.5 million. The ISO forecast sugar production in the European Union at 17.0 million tonnes, unchanged from the previous year. Brazilian output was also seen unchanged at 14.0 million tonnes.
India's sugar production would fall to 16.0 million tonnes from 17.7 million in 1995/96 and Thailand would produce 6.8 million after a previous 6.4 million, the ISO said.
Cuba would continue its recovery and produce 5.1 million tonnes in 1996/97 after 1995/96 output of 4.6 million.
China's output would fall 900,000 tonnes to 7.5 million.
Eastern Europe's two largest beet sugar producers, Ukraine and Russia, were expected to produce less in 1996/97.
Ukraine's output would total 3.2 million tonnes, 700,000 tonnes down on last year, and Russia's output was pegged at 1.9 million tonnes, 300,000 tonnes lower than in 1995/96.
Full details of the ISO's latest supply/demand estimates will be issued in mid-October.
